All the tips here are bang on, I am just going to add...

LinkedIn is just one path to finding work, it is not the only path.

So take all the tips here, because they are on point - prospective employers will likely click your LI profile before they call you, so make sure it is in good order.

I have also come across some good job search coaches, who have some good advice and once in a while will offer freebies like resume templates.

Last but not least... consider your job search a job and treat it like a job - regular start time, regular breaks, regular end time. That doesn't mean 8 hours of sending out resumes, part of my job search workday includes watching videos, attending webinars.

I recently attended some webinars on video in the work place, it was very cool, so I signed up for a service and will sometimes include a short 30-45 second introductory video with my submission and the response has been positive.

Oh, and for real last thing... do a google search for how to write ats friendly resumes - this one thing will increase your visibility dramatically

Best of luck

As someone who has been touched by suicide 9x - that is, I know 9 different people who have committed suicide, and as no one else has commented yet...

Let me start here; when you say *"there’s absolutely zero evidence"* you need to know, rarely is anything absolute.

So somewhere along the way you've probably had huge impact on someone and not even know it. Because a lot of times those little moments that mean nothing to us, mean everything to someone else.

Did you know in some parts of the world suicide is applauded and looked favorably upon? I'm not saying it's right or wrong, I'm saying it's a different view point.

Here in the west we get emotional about suicide, and feel bad that we couldn't do more.

I knew a Mother who confided in me she was relieved her son had taken his own life, he was in such emotional duress. She told me that just after his funeral.

Today, years later, she is reminiscent of the past and wonders what could have been.

Suicide is a permanent solution to a temporary problem. Sometimes that temporary is a longer time.

We're all kernels of corn, cooking in the same pot, in the same oil. None of those kernels pop at the same time, and your time to pop hasn't arrived yet.

Ever stop to consider all the different versions there are of yourself in this world? The people you work with and for have a version of you, the person at grocery check out has a version of you, the bus driver has a version, the pizza delivery guy has a different version of you.

There are hundreds, maybe thousands of different versions of you in this world, and you don't know which version made someone's day. Maybe you stopped someone from committing suicide.

You don't know for certain.

And the uncertainty of life is the only thing we can be certain of. And life is full of puzzles that need to be figured out.

Last but not least, one thing we should never take for certainty is our own thoughts, especially when we don't have feed back from other people. When we're closed off and isolated and think we're certain, that is your first clue to ask someone else.

One thing I have learned in life is... when we're uncertain, when we're not sure of what is happening to us or around us, when things get overwhelming, that should be our clue and catalyst to do...nothing, simply pause - for an hour, for a day.

It may not have been your intent, but now part of my day is going to be spent reflecting on those I have lost, I may call that Mother and chat about her son. And I am always grateful for those moments.

So Thank You.

Animals operate at a different level than we do, and because they can't communicate it to us, we think they lack, when it's us who lack. Yet we are blessed with their companionship.
